back: Very high, high, intermediate, low, very low: ordered by the amount of warming by 2100 (about 4.4 °C down to about 1.4 °C in IPCC AR6, rounded).
Greenhouse gases added to the atmosphere are balanced by those removed; needed to stop CO2-driven warming from increasing.
Greenhouse gases last for centuries and the deep ocean and ice sheets respond slowly, so sea level keeps rising after 2100.
Warm air holds about 7% more water vapour per 1 °C of warming; heavy rainfall becomes more intense, wet areas wetter, dry areas drier.
Melting ice exposes dark water or land, which absorbs more radiation, causing more warming and melting.
Ground at or below 0 °C for at least two years; thaw releases carbon dioxide and methane and makes ground unstable.
Warmer water (coral bleaching), sea-level rise and coastal flooding, ocean acidification, weaker overturning circulation.
The oceans have absorbed more than 90% of the extra heat in the climate system.
The Arctic is warming at least twice as fast as the global average, partly because of the albedo feedback.
